title: UI craft
summary: Rules for making app screens, dashboards, forms and sites look designed rather than AI-generated, plus a redesign audit.
benefit: Screens and pages look designed by a person, and redesigns follow a checklist.
solves: Screens that look AI-generated: purple gradients, identical cards and the same shadow under everything.
use_cases: Building or restyling an app screen, dashboard, form, website or HTML report, in any stack.
"Review this screen": Claude looks at a screenshot, lists what is wrong and fixes it in passes.
Your project has a design system (Angular Material, PrimeNG, tokens): it is kept and worked inside.
A good screen gets "it is fine" plus at most 2-3 refinements, never change for its own sake.
Concrete rules: one accent colour, a 4px spacing scale, a label above every field, one main chart.
details: When you design, build, redesign or review a UI in code, Claude applies rules that keep screens, dashboards, forms and sites looking designed rather than generated: quiet chrome, one accent, spacing on a 4px scale, clear hierarchy and states, plus a redesign audit. Use it in any stack, from Angular and React to plain HTML, and the project's own design system wins where one exists. It installs as a skill that loads only when used; instructions only, no code, no packages and no network.
risk: Instructions only; loads when used. No code runs on its own.
